classification.difficultyReason: The task requires constructing the intersection of four corner-centred disks and discovering a workable geometric decomposition, including its intersection lengths and circular-segment angles.

content.prompt: A point is chosen uniformly inside a square of side length $x$. Find the probability that the point is at distance no greater than $x$ from every corner of the square.

answer.short:
$1-\sqrt{3}+\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

Divide the area of the intersection of the four quarter circles by the square’s area.
answer.worked:
The required region is the intersection of four quarter circles of radius $x$, centred at the square’s corners. Its four boundary vertices form a square with diagonals $(\sqrt{3}-1)x$. Between adjacent vertices, each boundary arc subtends $30^\circ$ at its centre.

The area consists of this inner square and four circular segments. Each segment is a $30^\circ$ sector minus the triangle formed by its two radii.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{square}}&=\frac12\bigl((\sqrt{3}-1)x\bigr)^2\\A_{\text{square}}&=(2-\sqrt{3})x^2\\A_{\text{segment}}&=\frac{30}{360}\pi x^2-\frac12x^2\sin30^\circ\\A_{\text{segment}}&=\left(\frac{\pi}{12}-\frac14\right)x^2\\A_{\text{region}}&=(2-\sqrt{3})x^2+4\left(\frac{\pi}{12}-\frac14\right)x^2\\A_{\text{region}}&=\left(1-\sqrt{3}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)x^2\\\Pr(E)&=\frac{A_{\text{region}}}{x^2}\\\Pr(E)&=1-\sqrt{3}+\frac{\pi}{3}.\end{align*}$$
